Quit whining, grow up, and start acting like responsible adults and not spoiled little brats.

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kalsotra gives very in depth lectures. All of the information found on the exam come from the lectures so it is very important to attend each class. The professor does a great job at connecting the material to high yield topics on the MCAT, so if you are pre-med, you will be prepared. Dr. Kalsotra's office hours are also very helpful.

Professor Kalsotra was an amazing lecturer. I personally loved his Amino Acid Biosynthesis and metabolic integration units. He made biochemistry more interesting, so it became easy to study. It wasn't one of those classes that were hard yet boring; it was one of those classes that were hard but interesting to learn because of his teaching style.

Kalsotra was a great lecturer and it is clear he wants his students to succeed. He was often available for office hours multiple times a week. These sessions were extremely helpful. He was always very eager to answer any questions we had. Highly recommend reviewing his lecture slides, everything you need to know will be on there.

354 was the first biochem course I ever took, and I am glad it was Dr. Kalsotra who taught it. He truly wants you to succeed, and his efforts are seen in his preparation for lectures. He made the concepts easy to understand and connected them to real-world examples. He is also very approachable, and I had no problems asking him questions anytime.

Dr. Kalsotra is one of my favorite professors! His half of the semester was great-- the second half of biochemistry content wise was much harder, with extremely dense content-- but he does a great job of breaking down each step in a digestable format. He's clearly very passionate about teaching, and his lectures made biochemistry very enjoyable!

Prof. Boppart clearly knows what she's talking about. Some people might think of her as hard to approach or scary, but once you talk to her you realize this is not the case. Great lecturer, very knowledgeable. Only downside is little to no extra credit, and quizzes can make or break your grade (missing a question drops your grade to a 75%). Great at explaining difficult concepts but tends to be quite monotone in lectures. Offers review sessions and appointments to discuss grades if/when struggling.

Random quizzes worth 10 points about 15 over the semester.  Lab homework isn't pretty easy, lab only meets every other week. Do good on labs and set for at least a B. PHIL 100 is a writing intensive and if you go to office hours the (800w) papers should be easy enough. The quizzes in discussion can be tricky, so do well on them because those and the papers are your only graded assignments.

It's very clear how passionate Prof. Noel is towards the subject of philosophy. That being said, I did have many times in class where I felt I was not getting what I needed from his lectures due to allowing a lot of students to speak. While in-class opinions are valuable, it often impeded with my learning and understanding of the topics we discuss.

He was a great teacher who cares about his students and their opinions. There are 3 papers and a couple small assignments, but nothing overwhelming. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would recommend going!
